source.title: [re:DEFINICIJA] Vedran Politeo: Iscjeljenje nakon iskustva pobačaja je MOGUĆE

summary.title_hr: [re:DEFINICIJA] Vedran Politeo: Iscjeljenje nakon iskustva pobačaja je MOGUĆE
summary.abstract_hr: U epizodi podcasta Redefinicija gost je Vedran Politeo, dugogodišnji član inicijative "40 dana za život" i provoditelj programa "Iscjeljenje očeva srca". Govori o svom životu prije obraćenja, o pobačaju koji je doživio s tadašnjom partnericom i o tome kako je nakon obraćenja i ispovijedi pronašao oprost. Opisuje svoje dugogodišnje služenje u inicijativi, u kojoj je upoznao suprugu Antoniju, te objašnjava kako izgleda program za muškarce koji su imali namjerni ili spontani pobačaj. Razgovor se dotiče i izazova očinstva te obiteljske molitve. Završava porukom nade muškarcima koji se bore s posljedicama pobačaja: nisu sami i može im biti bolje.
key_points: Vedran je odrastao u obitelji koja nije bila praktično vjernička. Nakon pobačaja koji je doživio s tadašnjom partnericom veza se raspala jer su izgubili međusobno povjerenje.
Obratio se 5 do 6 godina nakon pobačaja, nakon teške situacije na poslu u kojoj je prvi put zavapio Bogu. Kaže da je ispovijedi za prvu pričest osjetio da mu je teret skinut i da mu je oprošteno.

U inicijativu "40 dana za život" nije došao kako bi se iskupio za pobačaj, nego zato što je tražio gdje će služiti. Ističe da mu vlastito iskustvo pomaže da bude bliži muškarcima koji dolaze na program.

Program "Iscjeljenje očeva srca" čine duhovne vježbe utemeljene na Svetom pismu i odnosu s Bogom Ocem. Uključuje veliku životnu ispovijed, a za muškarce se provodi individualno kroz pet susreta, dok se za žene održavaju trodnevni seminari.
Program je namijenjen i muškarcima koji su imali spontani pobačaj, jer i on nosi ranu, često praćenu samooptuživanjem.
Prema gostu, muškarci se rjeđe javljaju jer žele sve riješiti sami i rijetko jedni s drugima razgovaraju o pobačaju. Uz to, informacija o programu teško dopire do ljudi.
Svoju suprugu Antoniju upoznao je moleći krunicu na mjestu bdjenja ispred Vinogradske bolnice. Kao najveći izazov očinstva navodi pronalaženje ravnoteže između milosrđa i strogosti.
key_points_en: Vedran grew up in a family that was not practically religious. After the abortion he experienced with his partner at the time, the relationship fell apart because they lost mutual trust.

He converted 5 to 6 years after the abortion, following a difficult situation at work in which he cried out to God for the first time. He says that in confession for First Communion he felt that the burden was lifted from him and that he was forgiven.

He did not come to the initiative "40 dana za život" to make amends for the abortion, but because he was looking for a place to serve. He emphasizes that his own experience helps him be closer to the men who come to the program.

The program "Iscjeljenje očeva srca" consists of spiritual exercises based on Sacred Scripture and the relationship with God the Father. It includes a general life confession, and for men it is conducted individually through five meetings, while three-day seminars are held for women.
The program is also intended for men who have experienced a spontaneous abortion, because it too bears a wound, often accompanied by self-blame.

According to the guest, men reach out less often because they want to resolve everything on their own and rarely talk to one another about abortion. In addition, information about the program reaches people with difficulty.
He met his wife Antonija while praying the Rosary at the vigil site in front of Vinogradska bolnica. As the greatest challenge of fatherhood, he cites finding a balance between mercy and strictness.
summary.title_en: [re:DEFINICIJA] Vedran Politeo: Healing After the Experience of Abortion Is POSSIBLE
summary.abstract_en: In this episode of the Redefinicija podcast, the guest is Vedran Politeo, a long-time member of the initiative "40 dana za život" and facilitator of the program "Iscjeljenje očeva srca". He speaks about his life before conversion, about the abortion he experienced with his partner at the time, and about how, after conversion and confession, he found forgiveness. He describes his many years of service in the initiative, where he met his wife Antonija, and explains what the program looks like for men who have experienced an induced or spontaneous abortion. The conversation also touches upon the challenges of fatherhood and family prayer. It ends with a message of hope for men struggling with the consequences of abortion: they are not alone and they can get better.
